standard_text: The solar system: the Sun, planets, moons, asteroids and comets. Beyond the solar system: stars, the Milky Way galaxy, galaxies, light years. Looking into space with optical and radio telescopes, including SALT and MeerKAT/SKA in South Africa. (summary of CAPS Natural Sciences, Grade 8, Planet Earth and Beyond: The solar system; beyond the solar system; looking into space)
meta_desc: Free Grade 8 Natural Sciences worksheets (CAPS): the Sun and planets, scale of the solar system, stars, galaxies and light years, and telescopes. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: The Sun is one star in the Milky Way galaxy.

body_html:
How to think about it

The solar system is the Sun, eight planets, dwarf planets, moons, asteroids and comets. The inner planets are rocky; the outer planets are gas and ice giants. Gravity keeps the planets in orbit around the Sun.

The Sun is one of billions of stars in the Milky Way galaxy, and the universe has billions of galaxies. Distances are measured in light years, the distance light travels in a year. Optical telescopes such as SALT and radio telescopes such as MeerKAT and the Square Kilometre Array (SKA) in the Karoo help us study space.

Example

What keeps the planets in orbit?

A force of attraction

Answer: the Sun's gravity

Example

What does a light year measure?

It is not a time.

Answer: distance

Common mistakes

  • Thinking a light year is a unit of time.
  • Thinking the Sun is the biggest star.
  • Thinking stars are close to us.
